definition: Amorous means showing romantic love or attraction.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word amorous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know amorous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The novel's two lighthouse keepers grow openly amorous by the final chapters, signaling their affection across the bay each night.
Fond is far milder than amorous — you can be fond of a cousin or a corner café, while amorous behavior announces romantic attraction.
Besotted goes further than amorous — an amorous suitor writes the letters, while a besotted one can no longer think about anything else.

Romantic is broader and softer than amorous: it can describe people, but also moods, settings, and stories. Amorous stays with behavior — the visible showing of love: glances, courtship, letters. A place or a film can be romantic; only people (or courting swans) act amorous.

Smitten catches the falling itself — suddenly and completely taken with someone, often before a word is spoken. Amorous is about the outward display of love once it exists: the glances and courtship a bystander can see. You can be secretly smitten; amorous behavior is never secret.

Cleaning out the attic, Maya found a shoebox of her grandfather's letters from 1952, tied with kitchen string.
She expected stiff, formal notes.
Instead the letters were openly amorous: pressed violets in the folds, jokes about stolen glances at the library, and closing lines that grew bolder month by month.
Her grandmother, it turned out, had saved every one, numbering them in pencil in the corner.
The strange part was that no one in the family had ever seen the two of them so much as hold hands.
All that visible courtship, Maya realized, had simply moved indoors over the years — folded into a box, but never thrown away.
